newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Indonesian group to take over Cameroon rubber co.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian group to take over Cameroon rubber co.

text.p: Indonesian group PANWELL is to take over Cameroon's state rubber producing company HEVECAM with plans to double output to 50,000 tonnes a year, a government statement said.
GMG Investment, a subsidiary of Singapore-based PANWELL, will take a 90-percent stake in HEVECAM, after the largest privatisation offer since the government launched the campaign in 1990.
French company Terre Rouge, another company with rubber interests in the region, was also reported to be interested.
The statement said GMG Investment would pay 23 billion CFA francs for the stake and over 15 years would repay debts to the state worth the equivalent of 25 billion CFA.
GMG Investment plans to invest 31 billion CFA and create 3,000 new jobs as part of efforts to boost output and support development of 11,000 hectares of village rubber plantations.

PANWELL, which has interests ranging from banking, insurance and property to trade and farming, operates in Asia, the United States and Africa. It already has interests in rubber plantations in Nigeria and Ivory Coast.
Government and PANWELL representatives signed a preliminary agreement on Friday. A final agreement is expected to be signed by mid-December.

The World Bank made a $150 million structural adjustment loan to help relaunch the private sector conditional on transparent settlement of the HEVECAM sale. The Bank and IMF have accused Cameroon of dragging its feet over privatisation. ($1=508 CFA francs)
